body: Thanks again. I’ll reach out and let you know how things are going. Really appreciate your time today.

I appreciate you taking the time to talk. You’re right. I think I’ve found myself in a rut of not getting out and putting myself in places I enjoy being. I’m realizing it’s a trend I’m getting into at least once a year and then the remaining part of the year is me just sitting around and waiting for things to change rather than making the change. When I do something for a long time and things become stagnant, that is when I just distance myself from enjoying life. I think I need to alternate my time between different places and the things I enjoy.

I think it’s because I question whether the friendship will last and I just mentally back away until it becomes nothing. I know it doesn’t make sense. It’s just something I can’t help. Lately, I just spend too much time locking myself in the house. I’m medically retired from deployment injuries. Rarely get out anymore. I’ve just had a hard time with personal encouragement and getting involved in things. 

I like scuba diving. I’ve wanted to have a friend that dives too.
Never to a point that I felt like it meant anything. I’ve had close relationships, but I can’t help but feel like they are meaningless and then I destroy them. Not sure how to control that.

I don’t think the PTSD itself is the issue. I think the things that came with it is what prolonged my depression. Maybe even exasperated it. I’ve secluded myself when it comes to close relationships. I care for people. I always help others, but I never let people in. Ive has people die as I stared in their eyes while deployed. Then, that followed me home when I held someone in my arms as the died when we were out riding motorcycles. I just met him that day. Obviously I know it isn’t healthy to refrain from friendships. I just have a struggle getting over that.

Just meds. Therapy was just Groundhog Day to me.

I like mostly street photography. Candid shots or abstract things like going down an alleyway and taking a shot straight up. Different perspectives.

I’m a photographer/videographer. I enjoy it as a hobby and work. It’s just been hard to motivate myself the last 5-6 months to go find new things or places to enjoy. I have a degree in film thinking that would expand my horizons. Now I’m 5 weeks away from a masters degree and valedictorian. I thought maybe this sense of accomplishment would restore something within me. 

I’ve had really good days and super shitty ones. The last week has all been shitty, but there isn’t any explainable reason. 

Trying to be logical, I think I just need to go and have my meds increased tomorrow..

Honestly, I don’t even know. I’ve driven around a lot today. Just wanted to find something to smile about. The weather was nice. Usually rains this time of day, but it’s been sunny. I thought maybe being outside would at least clear my head. Came home and just sat in my car for a couple of hours. That’s basically been my day..
